notes: BATCH_006 Computer Knowledge part: 100 original, mostly scenario-based questions (BANK_COMP_000503 to BANK_COMP_000602) with two shared data tables (STIM_COMP_006001 SQL Loans table, STIM_COMP_006002 Excel deposits sheet). Computable answers (fractional binary, hex code space, 0.1 + 0.2 float error, weighted CPI, SSTF/FCFS disk-head movement, photo capacity, Mbps to MB/s, Hamming check bits, route summarisation, propagation delay, OTP guess probability, key counts, XOR cipher, SQL via sqlite3, Excel AVERAGEIF/RANK.EQ/COUNTIF and date difference) are re-derived in tools/batch_006/computer.py. Alt+Tab, Safe Mode, mv, sudo, AVERAGEIF, RANK.EQ, COUNTIF with &, Excel date serials, Data Validation, Word TOC, PowerPoint kiosk mode, WebSocket (RFC 6455), Access-Control-Allow-Origin, IPv4 TTL (RFC 791) and the MITRE ATT&CK descriptions of watering hole, MFA fatigue and password spraying were checked on the cited pages on 2026-11-05; the OEM licence rule, UPI Lite, IIN and MDR were confirmed from search results only (web:search-confirmed).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank's data-analytics officer needs a powerful single-user desktop computer with a fast multi-core processor, a large RAM and a professional graphics card to run heavy statistical models on his own desk. Which type of computer is this?

solution.explanation: A workstation is a high-performance computer meant for one user doing technical or analytical work such as modelling, CAD or video editing. It is more powerful than an ordinary office PC but is still a single-user desk machine.
steps: Single user + very high performance + on the desk = workstation
solution.why_others_wrong: A mainframe serves thousands of users from a data centre. A thin client has little processing power and depends on a server. An embedded computer is built into another device for one fixed task.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An interest rate of 0.75 is to be stored in binary. Which binary fraction is exactly equal to the decimal number 0.75?

solution.explanation: Multiply the fraction by 2 repeatedly and take the whole-number parts: 0.75 x 2 = 1.5 (digit 1), 0.5 x 2 = 1.0 (digit 1), and the remainder is 0. So 0.75 = 0.11 in binary, i.e. 1/2 + 1/4.
solution.shortcut: Place values after the binary point are 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 ...; 0.75 = 1/2 + 1/4.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank gives each of its terminals an ID made of exactly 4 hexadecimal digits (0-9, A-F), for example 0A7F. How many different terminal IDs are possible?

solution.concept: Counting codes in a number system
solution.explanation: Each hexadecimal digit can take 16 values, and the 4 positions are independent, so the number of codes is 16 x 16 x 16 x 16 = 16^4 = 65,536 (0000 to FFFF). This equals 2^16, because each hex digit stands for 4 bits.
solution.why_others_wrong: 64 multiplies 16 by 4 instead of raising it to the power 4. 4,096 is for 3 digits and 1,048,576 for 5.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A programmer adds 0.1 and 0.2 in a program that uses standard binary floating-point numbers, and the result prints as 0.30000000000000004 instead of 0.3. What is the reason?

options.text: 0.1 and 0.2 have no exact finite binary representation, so they are stored as close approximations
The processor's adder circuit is faulty and must be replaced
Floating-point numbers can store only whole numbers exactly, so every fraction is rounded to an integer
The result overflowed the largest number that a floating-point variable can hold

solution.concept: Representation error in binary floating point
solution.explanation: Just as 1/3 becomes 0.333... in decimal, 1/10 becomes a never-ending repeating fraction in binary (0.000110011...). A float keeps only a fixed number of bits, so 0.1 and 0.2 are stored as tiny approximations, and their sum is not exactly the stored value nearest to 0.3. This is why money is usually handled with decimal types or as whole paise.
steps: Rounding errors show up in the sum
solution.why_others_wrong: The hardware works correctly; this is a representation limit. Floats do store fractions, only not every fraction exactly. The values are far below the overflow limit.
solution.final_answer: Option A: 0.1 and 0.2 have no exact finite binary representation, so they are stored as close approximations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An old branch PC has a keyboard whose plug is round with six small pins and is usually colour-coded purple. Which port is this keyboard meant for?

solution.explanation: PS/2 is a round 6-pin mini-DIN connector used on older PCs for keyboards (purple) and mice (green). USB has largely replaced it.
solution.why_others_wrong: HDMI carries digital video and audio, RJ-45 is the Ethernet network connector, and VGA is a 15-pin D-shaped analog video port.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A teller's laptop becomes very hot when its cooling vents are blocked by files, and the processor automatically lowers its clock speed so that its temperature stays within safe limits. What is this behaviour called?

solution.explanation: When a processor reaches its temperature limit, it reduces its clock speed (and voltage) to produce less heat. This protects the chip but makes the computer slower until it cools down.
steps: Too hot -> processor slows itself = thermal throttling
solution.why_others_wrong: Overclocking raises the clock above the rated speed. Hyper-Threading runs two threads on one core. Pipelining overlaps the stages of several instructions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: One disk in a bank's file server fails. The technician pulls the failed disk out of its front bay and inserts a new one while the server keeps running and users stay connected. Which capability of the drive bays and interface allows this?

solution.explanation: Hot swapping (hot plugging) means a component can be removed and replaced while the system is powered on. Server drive bays with SAS/SATA backplanes support it, usually together with RAID so that no data is lost when a disk is removed.
steps: Replace a part while the system runs = hot swap
solution.why_others_wrong: A cold boot starts a computer from power-off. Overclocking speeds up a processor. Defragmentation rearranges file pieces on a hard disk.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Almost all smartphones, including those used for mobile banking, use processors based on a RISC instruction-set architecture known for low power use. Which architecture is it?

solution.explanation: ARM is a RISC architecture whose designs are licensed to many chip makers. Its energy efficiency makes it the standard for smartphones and tablets.
solution.why_others_wrong: x86-64 is the CISC architecture of most desktop and laptop PCs. z/Architecture is used in IBM mainframes. Itanium was a server architecture that has been discontinued.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In a program, 50% of executed instructions are ALU operations taking 1 clock cycle each, 30% are load/store instructions taking 2 cycles, and 20% are branches taking 3 cycles. What is the average CPI (cycles per instruction)?

solution.explanation: Average CPI is the sum of (fraction of instructions x cycles) over all instruction classes: 0.5 x 1 + 0.3 x 2 + 0.2 x 3 = 0.5 + 0.6 + 0.6 = 1.7.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2.0 is the simple average of 1, 2 and 3, ignoring how often each class occurs. 1.5 and 1.9 come from arithmetic slips.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In a pipelined processor, the instruction ADD R1, R2, R3 is immediately followed by SUB R4, R1, R5. SUB needs the new value of R1 before ADD has written it back. What kind of pipeline problem is this?

solution.explanation: A data hazard arises when an instruction depends on the result of an earlier instruction still in the pipeline. Here SUB reads R1 after ADD writes it (RAW). It is handled by forwarding the result or by stalling.
steps: Second instruction needs first one's result = data dependency
solution.why_others_wrong: A structural hazard is two instructions needing the same hardware unit at once. A control hazard comes from branches. Cache coherence concerns copies of data in several processors' caches.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Data hazard (read after write)

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In a loop, the processor reaches a conditional jump before the condition has been worked out. Instead of waiting, it guesses which way the jump will go from its past behaviour and starts fetching instructions on that path; if the guess is wrong, those instructions are discarded. What is this technique called?

solution.explanation: A branch predictor records how branches behaved before and predicts the next outcome. Correct guesses keep the pipeline busy; a wrong guess flushes the speculatively fetched instructions.
steps: Guess the direction of a conditional jump = branch prediction
solution.why_others_wrong: Operand forwarding passes a result directly to a waiting instruction. DMA moves data between a device and memory without the CPU. Interrupt handling responds to device signals.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An interest program compiles without errors. While it is running, it crashes with a 'division by zero' message when it processes a branch that has no accounts. What type of error is this?

solution.explanation: A runtime error occurs only while the program is executing, when an operation becomes impossible, such as dividing by zero or opening a missing file. The program was syntactically correct, so it compiled.
steps: Compiled fine, failed while running = runtime error
solution.why_others_wrong: Syntax and compilation errors stop the program from being compiled at all. A linker error occurs when the parts of a program are combined, before it runs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A new laptop is bought with Windows already installed by the laptop maker. Its licence is tied to that laptop and cannot be moved to another computer. What type of licence is this?

solution.explanation: An OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) licence comes pre-installed by the hardware maker. It is bound to the device it first ships with and generally has no transfer rights.
steps: Pre-installed by maker + tied to device = OEM licence
solution.why_others_wrong: A site licence covers many computers at one organisation's premises. An open-source licence lets users see and change the code. Public domain software has no copyright at all.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft small-business blog: OEM Windows licences have no transfer rights and stay with the computer they were shipped with and installed on.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A branch officer adds a small add-on to her web browser that blocks pop-up advertisements. The add-on works only inside the browser and extends what the browser can do. What is such software called?

solution.explanation: An extension or plug-in is a small program that adds a feature to a host application such as a browser. It cannot run on its own.
steps: Adds a feature to the browser = extension / plug-in
solution.why_others_wrong: A device driver lets the OS control hardware. The operating system manages the whole computer. Firmware is stored in a device's chip and controls its basic functions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A developer wants to stop a loan program at a chosen line, run it one statement at a time and watch how the value of a variable changes, to find a bug. Which tool should she use?

solution.explanation: A debugger lets a programmer set breakpoints, step through code line by line and inspect or watch variables while the program runs, which helps locate logic and runtime errors.
steps: Breakpoints + step through + watch variables = debugger
solution.why_others_wrong: A linker joins object files into one executable, an assembler translates assembly language into machine code, and a loader copies a program into memory to run it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A function to find the balance after n years is written as: balance(n) = balance(n - 1) x 1.07, with balance(0) = the opening deposit. The function calls itself with a smaller value of n until n reaches 0. What is this programming technique called?

solution.explanation: A recursive function solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of the same problem, and stops at a base case (here n = 0).
steps: Function calls itself + base case = recursion
solution.why_others_wrong: Encapsulation hides an object's data behind its methods. Inheritance lets a class reuse another class's members. Compilation translates source code into machine code.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Ten programmers work on the same banking app. The team needs software that records every change to the source files, shows who changed what, lets each person work on a separate branch, and can bring back any earlier version. Which kind of tool is this?

options.text: Version control system such as Git

solution.explanation: A version control system keeps the full history of a project's files, supports branches and merging, and lets the team compare or restore any earlier version. Git is the most widely used.
steps: Track changes, branches, restore old versions = version control
solution.why_others_wrong: A compiler translates code but keeps no change history. A spreadsheet is an application for tables of numbers. A defragmenter rearranges file pieces on a hard disk.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Version control system such as Git

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A budgeting app can be used free of charge forever with its basic features, with no time limit. Advanced features such as detailed reports are unlocked only after paying for a premium plan. What is this business model called?

solution.explanation: Freemium (free + premium) gives a basic version free permanently and charges for extra features or capacity.
steps: Free basic version forever + paid extras = freemium
solution.why_others_wrong: Shareware is a trial that must be bought after the trial period. Freeware is fully free with no paid tier. Public domain software has no copyright owner.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Several programs on a Windows server use the same library file (a .dll file). The library is not copied into each program; it is loaded when a program runs, so replacing the one library file fixes a bug in all of them. What is this method of linking called?

solution.explanation: With dynamic linking, the library code (a DLL on Windows, a .so file on Linux) stays in a separate file and is attached when the program is loaded or run. Programs share it and get its updates automatically. Static linking copies the library code into each executable at build time.
steps: Library loaded at run time and shared = dynamic linking
solution.why_others_wrong: Static linking copies the code into every program, so each would need rebuilding. Cross-compilation produces code for another platform. Interpretation executes source code line by line.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A developer writes the software for an ATM's card-reader controller on his Windows PC. He compiles it on the PC into machine code for the controller's different (ARM) processor and then loads it onto the device. What kind of compiler is he using?

solution.explanation: A cross-compiler runs on one platform (the host) and produces executable code for a different platform (the target). It is standard for embedded devices that are too small to compile code themselves.
steps: Compile on machine A, run on machine B with a different processor = cross-compiler
solution.why_others_wrong: An interpreter executes code directly without producing an executable. A decompiler turns machine code back into source-like code. A JIT compiler compiles while the program runs, on the same machine.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A cashier has the core banking screen, a calculator and an email window open on Windows. Which keyboard shortcut lets him switch quickly between these open windows?

solution.explanation: Alt + Tab switches between open windows; holding Alt and pressing Tab repeatedly cycles through them.
steps: Switch between open windows = Alt + Tab
solution.why_others_wrong: Ctrl + Z undoes the last action, Windows + L locks the computer, and Ctrl + P prints.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft: Alt + Tab switches between open windows; hold Alt and press Tab repeatedly to cycle through them.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: On a Linux server, an administrator wants to rename the file report.txt to report_2026.txt in the same folder. Which command does this?

solution.explanation: Linux has no separate rename command for this everyday task: mv (move) renames a file when the destination is a new name in the same directory, and moves it when the destination is another directory.
steps: Rename = move to a new name = mv old new
solution.why_others_wrong: cp makes a copy and leaves the original. rm deletes the files. cat displays file contents.

fact_checks.claim: Linux man page: mv - move (rename) files; rename SOURCE to DEST, or move SOURCE(s) to DIRECTORY.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A Linux user who is not logged in as root needs to install a software package, which requires administrative rights. Which command should he put before the install command so that it runs with superuser privileges, if the system's policy permits him?

solution.explanation: sudo lets a permitted user run a command as the superuser (or another user), as allowed by the security policy, usually after entering his own password. Every use can be logged.
steps: Run one command with admin rights = sudo command
solution.why_others_wrong: pwd prints the current directory, grep searches text, and chmod changes file permissions; none of them raises the user's privileges.

fact_checks.claim: sudo manual: sudo allows a permitted user to execute a command as the superuser or another user, as specified by the security policy.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: After a faulty printer driver was installed, a branch PC crashes during every normal start-up. The technician wants Windows to start with only a basic set of files and drivers so that he can remove the faulty driver. Which start-up mode should he use?

solution.explanation: Safe Mode starts Windows in a basic state with a limited set of files and drivers. If the problem does not appear in Safe Mode, default drivers and settings are not the cause, and the faulty driver can be removed.
steps: Start with minimal drivers to troubleshoot = Safe Mode
solution.why_others_wrong: Sleep mode pauses a running session in low power. Airplane mode turns off wireless radios. Tablet mode changes the interface for touch use.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft: Safe mode starts Windows in a basic state, using a limited set of files and drivers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: On Linux, the ls command does not show the configuration file .bashrc in a user's home directory, although the file exists. Which command will list it?

solution.explanation: In Linux, any file or directory whose name begins with a dot is hidden from a normal listing. ls -a (all) shows these hidden entries too.
solution.why_others_wrong: ls -l gives a long listing with permissions and sizes but still hides dot-files. pwd prints the current directory. mkdir creates a directory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A disk's read/write head is at cylinder 50. Requests are waiting for cylinders 82, 170, 43, 140, 24, 16 and 190 (in that order of arrival). Using SSTF (Shortest Seek Time First) disk scheduling, what is the total head movement in cylinders?

solution.explanation: SSTF always serves the pending request closest to the current head position. From 50: 43 (7), 24 (19), 16 (8), then the nearest is 82 (66), 140 (58), 170 (30), 190 (20). Total = 7 + 19 + 8 + 66 + 58 + 30 + 20 = 208 cylinders.
solution.why_others_wrong: 642 is the movement under FCFS, serving requests in arrival order. 174 counts only the upward sweep from 16, and 140 is just 190 - 50.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A training officer wants to show his PowerPoint slides on a large wall screen to 60 new recruits in a hall. Which output device should he connect to the laptop?

solution.explanation: A projector takes the computer's video signal and throws an enlarged image onto a screen or wall, so a large audience can see it.
steps: Large image for an audience = projector (output)
solution.why_others_wrong: A scanner, a webcam and a barcode reader are all input devices; they send data into the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A branch prints a customer's account statement on paper. Output that is produced in a permanent physical form such as paper is called:

solution.explanation: Hard copy is printed (physical) output, for example from a printer or plotter. Soft copy is output seen on a screen or stored as a file, which disappears from view when the display changes.
solution.why_others_wrong: Soft copy is on-screen or electronic. Source code is a program's text. A cache copy is temporary data kept for faster access.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: When a user types on a smartphone's on-screen keyboard, the phone gives a short vibration with each key press, so that the touch feels like pressing a real key. This kind of touch-based output is called:

solution.explanation: Haptic (tactile) feedback uses small vibration motors or actuators to give the user a sense of touch, such as a 'click' or a buzz to confirm an action.
steps: Output felt as vibration/touch = haptic feedback
solution.why_others_wrong: OCR converts images of text into editable text (input). Speech synthesis is spoken output. Refresh rate is how many times per second a display redraws its image.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In one kind of inkjet printer, the print head does not heat the ink. Instead, a crystal material changes shape when a voltage is applied, and this movement pushes each ink droplet out of the nozzle. What type of inkjet technology is this?

solution.explanation: Inkjet printers use one of two main methods. Thermal (bubble) inkjets heat the ink to form a bubble that forces a drop out. Piezoelectric inkjets use a crystal that flexes when voltage is applied, which pushes the drop out without heating the ink.
steps: Crystal flexes under voltage, no heating = piezoelectric inkjet
solution.why_others_wrong: A thermal inkjet heats the ink. A dot-matrix printer strikes an inked ribbon with pins. A laser printer uses a drum and toner.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A visually impaired bank officer reads screen text through a device placed below the keyboard, on which small pins rise and fall to form Braille characters that change as he moves through the document. What is this device?

solution.explanation: A refreshable Braille display is an output device. Screen-reader software sends text to it, and electronically controlled pins form Braille cells that the user reads by touch; the pins change as the text changes.
steps: Pins forming Braille from screen text = refreshable Braille display (output)
solution.why_others_wrong: An optical mark reader reads marked bubbles on forms. A graphics tablet and a light pen are input devices for drawing or pointing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: When a customer turns her phone sideways, the banking app switches from portrait to landscape view. Which built-in input sensor detects the change in the phone's orientation from the direction of gravity?

solution.explanation: An accelerometer measures acceleration along three axes, including the constant pull of gravity, so the phone can tell which way it is being held and rotate the screen. A gyroscope often helps with rotation.
solution.why_others_wrong: A proximity sensor detects an object near the screen (e.g. the ear during a call). An ambient light sensor adjusts brightness. A fingerprint sensor authenticates the user.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A branch saves scanned documents to an online service so that they are stored on the provider's remote servers and can be opened from any computer through the internet. What is this type of storage called?

solution.explanation: Cloud storage keeps files on servers run by a provider, reached over the internet. Users can access them from many devices, and the provider handles backup of the hardware.
steps: Files on remote servers via internet = cloud storage
solution.why_others_wrong: Cache memory and registers are small, fast memories inside or near the CPU. ROM holds firmware on the computer itself.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A pen drive has 64 GB of free space. How many photos of exactly 4 MB each can it hold? (Use 1 GB = 1024 MB.)

solution.explanation: 64 GB = 64 x 1024 MB = 65,536 MB. Each photo uses 4 MB, so the drive holds 65,536 / 4 = 16,384 photos.
solution.why_others_wrong: 16,000 uses 1 GB = 1000 MB. 65,536 forgets to divide by the photo size. 2,048 divides by 32 instead of 4.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A clerk needs an optical disc on which backup files can be written, erased and written again many times. Which disc should he use?

solution.explanation: RW (ReWritable) discs can be erased and re-recorded many times. R discs can be written only once, and ROM discs come pre-recorded and cannot be written by the user.
steps: Write, erase and rewrite = RW disc
solution.why_others_wrong: CD-ROM and BD-ROM are read-only discs pressed at the factory. A CD-R can be written only once.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A branch PC becomes slow when the clerk keeps the core banking application, several browser tabs and a spreadsheet open together. Which upgrade most directly lets the PC hold more running programs at once?

options.text: Adding a larger hard disk for archives

solution.explanation: Running programs and their data must be held in RAM (main memory). With too little RAM, the system keeps moving data to and from disk, which slows it down. More RAM lets more programs stay in memory at once.
steps: Many programs open at once -> need more main memory -> add RAM
solution.why_others_wrong: Extra archive disk space does not help programs that are already running. The keyboard and monitor do not affect how many programs can be kept in memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A branch's internet connection is 100 Mbps (megabits per second). At full speed, how many megabytes of data can it download per second? (Take 1 byte = 8 bits.)

solution.concept: Bits and bytes in data rates
solution.explanation: Network speeds use bits (small b), file sizes use bytes (capital B). Dividing by 8 converts bits to bytes: 100 / 8 = 12.5 MB per second.
solution.why_others_wrong: 100 confuses megabits with megabytes. 800 multiplies by 8 instead of dividing. 1.25 divides by 80.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A video-editing PC stripes its data across two disks so that reads and writes are split between them and are faster, but there is no copy or parity: if either disk fails, all the data is lost. Which RAID level is this?

solution.explanation: RAID 0 (striping) spreads blocks across disks for speed and uses their full combined capacity, but it has no redundancy, so the failure of any one disk destroys the array.
solution.why_others_wrong: RAID 1 mirrors data on two disks. RAID 5 stripes with one disk's worth of parity and RAID 6 with two, so both survive disk failures.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Each flash memory cell in an SSD can be erased and rewritten only a limited number of times. The SSD's controller therefore spreads writes evenly across all its cells, so that no area wears out early. What is this technique called?

solution.explanation: Wear levelling maps logical blocks to different physical cells over time, so that writes are spread evenly and the drive lasts longer.
steps: Spread writes evenly over flash cells = wear levelling
solution.why_others_wrong: Defragmentation rearranges file pieces on hard disks and is not needed on SSDs. Mirroring copies data to a second disk. Low-level formatting prepares the physical surface of a disk.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A report-generation program runs for days on a server. Each run allocates RAM for temporary data but never releases it, so the program's memory use keeps rising until the server slows down and the program crashes. What is this fault called?

solution.explanation: A memory leak happens when a program keeps allocating memory but fails to free memory it no longer needs. Usage grows steadily until memory runs out. Restarting the program releases the memory, but the fix is in the code.
steps: Memory allocated, never freed, usage keeps growing = memory leak
solution.why_others_wrong: A buffer cache is a useful store of disk data in RAM. Thrashing is constant paging when RAM is too small for the working set, a possible effect but not the fault itself. Interleaving spreads addresses across memory banks for speed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A technician installs two identical 8 GB RAM modules in the matching coloured slots of a motherboard instead of one 16 GB module, so that the memory controller can access both modules at the same time and nearly double the memory bandwidth. Which feature is being used?

solution.explanation: In dual-channel mode, the memory controller uses two independent 64-bit channels in parallel, giving a 128-bit path to RAM and nearly double the bandwidth. Modules must be placed in the paired slots shown in the motherboard manual.
steps: Two matched modules in paired slots, accessed together = dual channel
solution.why_others_wrong: Virtual memory uses disk space as an extension of RAM. ECC memory detects and corrects bit errors. Write-back is a cache write policy.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A server's ECC memory uses a Hamming code that can correct any single-bit error in a 64-bit data word. For m data bits, the number of check bits r must satisfy 2^r >= m + r + 1. What is the smallest number of check bits needed?

solution.explanation: Try values of r. r = 6: 2^6 = 64, but 64 + 6 + 1 = 71, so 64 < 71 fails. r = 7: 2^7 = 128 and 64 + 7 + 1 = 72, so 128 >= 72 holds. Seven check bits are needed; adding one overall parity bit for double-error detection gives the familiar 72-bit ECC word (SECDED).
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 and 6 are too few (32 and 64 are less than the required 70 and 71). 8 is the SECDED total with the extra parity bit, not the minimum for single-error correction.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A customer applying for a loan online selects the scanned copy of her PAN card on her computer and sends it to the bank's website. Sending a file from your computer to a server on the internet is called:

solution.explanation: Uploading transfers a file from the local computer to a remote server. Downloading is the opposite: copying a file from a server to the local computer.
solution.why_others_wrong: Downloading copies data from the server to the computer. Browsing is viewing web pages. Bookmarking saves a page's address.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank updates its home page, but one employee keeps seeing the old version even after re-typing the address, while colleagues see the new page. The usual fix is to clear the browser's stored copies of recently visited pages and images. What are these stored copies called?

solution.explanation: Browsers keep local copies of pages, images and scripts in a cache so that sites load faster on later visits. If the cached copy is still used, the user sees outdated content until the cache is cleared or the page is reloaded fresh.
steps: Old stored copy of a page shown = browser cache
solution.why_others_wrong: History is only a list of visited addresses. Bookmarks are saved links. Plug-ins add features to the browser and do not store page copies.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In the address https://bank.example/locate?branch=pune&type=atm , what is the part branch=pune&type=atm (after the question mark) called?

solution.explanation: In a URL, the part after ? is the query string. It passes name=value pairs, joined by &, to the server, here asking for ATMs in Pune. https is the scheme, bank.example the domain name and /locate the path.
steps: After '?' = query string of name=value pairs joined by '&'
solution.why_others_wrong: The domain name is bank.example and the scheme is https. No port is written, so the default 443 is used.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: When a customer logs in to net banking, the server builds a page at that moment showing his own name, accounts and latest balance from the database. The same address shows different content to different customers. What kind of web page is this?

solution.explanation: A dynamic page is generated by the server (or by scripts) when it is requested, usually from a database, so its content changes with the user and time. A static page is a fixed file that everyone sees in the same form.
steps: Content built per request, differs per user = dynamic page
solution.why_others_wrong: A static page is the same for every visitor. A home page is a site's starting page, which may be static or dynamic. An offline page is a saved copy.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A regional office wants to send circulars to all 40 branch managers by typing a single address, such as branch-managers@bank.example, instead of entering 40 addresses each time. What is such a group address called?

solution.explanation: A distribution list (mailing list or contact group) is one name or address that stands for many members. A message sent to it is delivered to everyone on the list, and membership can be changed centrally.
steps: One address that reaches many members = distribution list
solution.why_others_wrong: Bcc hides recipients but still needs each address typed. A signature is text added at the end of messages. An auto-reply answers incoming mail automatically.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A share-trading screen must receive price updates pushed by the server the moment they change, and also send orders, over one long-lived two-way connection rather than repeatedly asking the server with new HTTP requests. Which protocol, standardised in RFC 6455, is designed for this?

solution.explanation: The WebSocket protocol starts with an HTTP handshake and then keeps a single TCP connection open, over which both client and server can send messages at any time. This suits live prices, chat and notifications.
solution.why_others_wrong: FTP transfers files, POP3 downloads email, and SNMP monitors and manages network devices.

fact_checks.claim: RFC 6455: the WebSocket Protocol enables two-way communication between a client and a remote host.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A script on https://partner.example tries to read data from an API at https://api.bank.example. Because the origins differ, the browser blocks the script from reading the response unless the bank's server sends a particular response header naming the allowed origin. Which header is it?

solution.explanation: Under CORS, a server lists which other origins may read its responses. The browser checks the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header and lets the script read the response only if the requesting origin is allowed.
steps: Cross-origin read permission = CORS header Access-Control-Allow-Origin
solution.why_others_wrong: Strict-Transport-Security forces HTTPS for a site. Set-Cookie stores a cookie. Content-Length gives the body size.

fact_checks.claim: MDN: the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header indicates whether the response can be shared with requesting code from the given origin.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank links the computers of all its branches and offices spread across one city, such as Pune, into a single network. A network covering a city is called a:

options.text: WAN (Wide Area Network) spanning several countries

solution.explanation: By area: a PAN covers a person's devices, a LAN one building or campus, a MAN a city, and a WAN large regions, countries or the world.
solution.why_others_wrong: A PAN links personal devices a few metres apart. A LAN covers one building or campus. A WAN spanning countries is much larger than one city.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank's data centre links two buildings with a cable that carries data as pulses of light through thin glass strands, so that it is unaffected by electrical interference and can run long distances at high speed. Which cable is this?

solution.explanation: Optical fibre sends data as light through glass or plastic cores. It offers very high bandwidth, long distances and immunity to electromagnetic interference.
steps: Light pulses through glass = optical fibre
solution.why_others_wrong: Coaxial, twisted-pair and telephone cables all carry electrical signals over copper and are affected by electrical interference.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Wi-Fi networks in bank branches follow a family of wireless LAN standards published by the IEEE. What is the number of this family of standards?

solution.explanation: IEEE 802.11 is the family of wireless LAN standards on which Wi-Fi is based (802.11n, ac, ax and so on).
solution.why_others_wrong: IEEE 802.3 is wired Ethernet, 802.15.1 is the basis of Bluetooth, and IEEE 1394 is FireWire.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which OSI layer provides end-to-end delivery between processes on two computers, using port numbers, segmentation of data and (with TCP) error recovery and flow control?

solution.explanation: The transport layer (layer 4) carries data between applications on the source and destination hosts. TCP and UDP work here, and port numbers identify the applications.
solution.why_others_wrong: The data link layer delivers frames on one link using MAC addresses. The physical layer sends raw bits. The presentation layer handles data format, encryption and compression.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A branch PC can print to the printer and open shared folders on its own LAN, but cannot reach any website or the head-office server outside the LAN. Its IP address and subnet mask are correct. Which setting is most likely missing or wrong?

solution.explanation: A host sends traffic for its own subnet directly, but traffic for any other network goes to the default gateway, normally the router's LAN address. If the gateway is missing or wrong, local access works while everything beyond the LAN fails.
steps: Local works, remote fails = no route out = check default gateway
solution.why_others_wrong: The MAC address is burned into the network card and local traffic already works. Screen resolution and printer drivers have nothing to do with reaching other networks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: With a walkie-talkie, both people can talk to each other, but only one at a time; each must wait until the other stops. Which data transmission mode does this represent?

solution.explanation: Simplex sends in one direction only (like TV broadcast). Half duplex allows both directions but not at the same time (walkie-talkie). Full duplex allows both directions at once (telephone call).
steps: Both ways, one at a time = half duplex
solution.why_others_wrong: Full duplex lets both talk at once. Simplex is one-way only. Multiplexing combines several signals on one channel and is not a direction mode.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A regional router learns four branch networks: 192.168.4.0/24, 192.168.5.0/24, 192.168.6.0/24 and 192.168.7.0/24. To keep the routing table small, they are to be advertised as one summary route that covers exactly these four networks. What is the summary route?

solution.explanation: Four /24 networks need 2 fewer prefix bits: /22. The third octets 4 to 7 are 000001 00 to 000001 11, so the first 6 bits of the third octet (000001) are common. The summary is 192.168.4.0/22, which covers 192.168.4.0 to 192.168.7.255.
solution.shortcut: A /22 block starts at a multiple of 4 in the third octet; 4 is a multiple of 4.
solution.why_others_wrong: /23 covers only 4.x and 5.x. 192.168.0.0/21 covers 0.x to 7.x, eight networks, more than required. /24 covers only 192.168.4.x.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A fibre link between two data centres is 2,000 km long, and signals travel through the fibre at 2 x 10^8 m/s. What is the one-way propagation delay?

solution.explanation: Propagation delay = distance / signal speed = (2,000 x 10^3 m) / (2 x 10^8 m/s) = 0.01 s = 10 ms. It depends on distance and the medium, not on the bandwidth of the link.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6.67 ms uses the speed of light in vacuum (3 x 10^8 m/s). 1 ms and 100 ms are out by a factor of 10.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A Wi-Fi radio cannot detect a collision while it is transmitting, because its own strong signal drowns out others. So before sending, it listens to the channel, waits a random back-off time, and relies on acknowledgements. Which media-access method does Wi-Fi use?

options.text: CSMA/CD (Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection)
CSMA/CA (Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance)

solution.explanation: Classic shared (half-duplex) Ethernet used CSMA/CD: transmit, detect a collision, stop and retry. Wireless stations cannot reliably detect collisions, so IEEE 802.11 uses CSMA/CA, avoiding collisions with carrier sensing, random back-off and acknowledgements (optionally RTS/CTS).
steps: Wireless cannot detect collisions -> avoid them
solution.why_others_wrong: CSMA/CD needs collision detection, which radios lack. Token passing was used in Token Ring networks. Polling is not the Wi-Fi access method.
solution.final_answer: Option B: CSMA/CA (Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance)

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Because of a routing mistake, packets between two routers keep going round in a loop. Which field in the IPv4 header makes sure that such a packet is eventually discarded instead of circulating forever?

solution.explanation: Every router that forwards an IPv4 packet decreases its TTL by at least 1. When the TTL reaches zero, the packet is destroyed (and an ICMP Time Exceeded message is usually sent back). The traceroute tool uses this behaviour.
solution.why_others_wrong: The header checksum detects header corruption. Type of Service marks priority. The source address identifies the sender. None limits the packet's lifetime.

fact_checks.claim: RFC 791: the Time to Live field must be decreased at each point that the internet header is processed; if it contains zero, the datagram must be destroyed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank connects its core switches with redundant links for reliability. Without protection, these loops would let broadcast frames circulate endlessly (a broadcast storm). Which protocol makes the switches block some links logically to form a loop-free tree, and re-enables them if an active link fails?

solution.explanation: STP (IEEE 802.1D, with the faster RSTP) elects a root bridge and puts redundant ports into a blocking state, so that exactly one active path exists between any two switches. If a link fails, a blocked port is moved to forwarding.
steps: Redundant switch links + loop prevention = STP
solution.why_others_wrong: ARP maps IP addresses to MAC addresses, DHCP assigns IP settings to hosts, and SMTP sends email.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: During a festival sale, a bank's net-banking website becomes unreachable because thousands of infected computers around the world send it a huge flood of requests at the same time. What is this attack called?

solution.explanation: A DDoS attack overloads a server or network with traffic from many sources, usually a botnet, so that genuine users cannot get service. It attacks availability rather than stealing data.
steps: Flood of traffic from many machines -> service down = DDoS
solution.why_others_wrong: Phishing tricks users into revealing data. Shoulder surfing watches someone type a PIN or password. Keylogging records keystrokes.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An attacker uses a program that tries every possible combination of characters, one after another, until it finds a user's password. What is this method called?

solution.explanation: A brute-force attack systematically tries all possible passwords. Long, complex passwords and account lockout after a few failed attempts make it impractical.
solution.why_others_wrong: Phishing tricks the user into giving the password. Tailgating is following someone through a secure door. Pharming redirects users to a fake site by tampering with DNS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which practice best allows a branch to recover its files after a ransomware attack without paying the attackers?

options.text: Saving all files on the same desktop for easy access
Keeping regular backups that are stored offline or separately from the network
Turning off the screen saver password
Sharing one administrator password among all staff

solution.explanation: Ransomware encrypts files on infected systems and on drives they can reach. Recent backups kept offline or isolated cannot be encrypted by the attack, so data can be restored after cleaning the systems.
steps: Restore from clean, separate backups instead of paying
solution.why_others_wrong: Keeping files on the desktop, removing screen-lock passwords and sharing admin passwords all make attacks easier, not recovery.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Keeping regular backups that are stored offline or separately from the network

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Attackers find that employees of several banks often visit a particular banking-industry news website. They secretly plant malicious code on that site, so that bank employees' computers get infected when they visit it. What is this attack called?

solution.explanation: In a watering hole attack, attackers compromise a legitimate website that their target group is known to visit, and wait for victims to come to it, like a predator waiting at a watering hole.
steps: Infect a site the target group visits = watering hole
solution.why_others_wrong: Vishing uses phone calls. Baiting leaves an infected device or tempting download for victims. Shoulder surfing is watching someone type.

fact_checks.claim: MITRE ATT&CK T1189: a targeted campaign using websites visited by a specific community is often referred to as a strategic web compromise or watering hole attack.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An attacker who has stolen an officer's password logs in again and again late at night, so that the officer's phone keeps receiving 'Approve sign-in?' push notifications. Hoping to stop the alerts, the officer finally taps Approve. What is this attack called?

solution.explanation: MFA fatigue abuses push-based MFA by flooding the user with approval requests until he approves one. Defences include number matching, limits on prompts and training users to report unexpected prompts.
steps: Has password + floods approval prompts until user accepts = MFA fatigue
solution.why_others_wrong: SIM swap takes over the victim's mobile number. Credential stuffing tries leaked passwords on many sites. Juice jacking abuses public USB charging ports.

fact_checks.claim: MITRE ATT&CK T1621: adversaries may bombard users with MFA push notifications, SMS messages and phone calls; repeatedly generating prompts until the user accepts is known as MFA fatigue.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A fraudster registers the domain examp1ebank.com (with the digit 1 in place of the letter l) to catch customers who mistype or misread the genuine examplebank.com, and sets up a look-alike login page there. What is this technique called?

solution.explanation: Typosquatting (URL hijacking) registers domain names that differ slightly from a real brand's domain, relying on typing mistakes or careless reading, and uses them for phishing or malware.
steps: Misspelt look-alike domain to catch users = typosquatting
solution.why_others_wrong: Cryptojacking mines cryptocurrency on victims' machines. A logic bomb is code triggered by a condition. A botnet is a network of infected computers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank locks an account after five wrong passwords. An attacker avoids this by trying the same two or three very common passwords against thousands of different customer accounts, so that no single account gets enough failures to be locked. What is this attack called?

solution.explanation: Password spraying tries one or a few common passwords across many accounts. It stays under per-account lockout limits, so detection must look at failures across accounts and sources.
steps: Few common passwords x many accounts, avoids lockout = password spraying
solution.why_others_wrong: A brute-force attack tries many passwords on one account and would trigger the lockout. Pharming redirects users through DNS tampering. A man-in-the-middle attack intercepts traffic.

fact_checks.claim: MITRE ATT&CK T1110.003: adversaries may use a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many different accounts to attempt to acquire valid account credentials.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A transaction OTP has 6 digits (000000 to 999999), each value equally likely, and the bank allows only 3 attempts. If a fraudster guesses 3 different values, what is the probability that one of them is correct?

solution.explanation: There are 10^6 = 1,000,000 possible 6-digit OTPs. Three different guesses cover 3 of them, so the chance of success is 3 / 1,000,000. Limiting attempts keeps this tiny.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1 in 1,000,000 is the chance with a single guess. 3 in 100,000 assumes 5 digits. 1 in 10,000 is for a single guess of a 4-digit code.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank's email security system opens suspicious attachments in an isolated virtual environment and watches what they do there before delivering them, so that malware cannot harm real systems. What is this technique called?

solution.explanation: A sandbox is a restricted, isolated environment in which untrusted code can run. Its behaviour (changing files, contacting servers) can be observed without risk to the real network.
steps: Run untrusted file in isolation and observe = sandboxing
solution.why_others_wrong: Defragmentation rearranges disk files, port forwarding redirects network traffic to an internal host, and spooling queues jobs such as print jobs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Ten branch servers must each be able to communicate privately with every other one. How many keys are needed if every pair shares its own secret symmetric key, and how many if each server instead has its own public-private key pair?

options.text: 90 secret keys with symmetric encryption; 10 keys with public-key encryption
10 secret keys with symmetric encryption; 45 keys with public-key encryption
45 secret keys with symmetric encryption; 20 keys (10 key pairs) with public-key encryption
20 secret keys with symmetric encryption; 20 keys (10 key pairs) with public-key encryption

solution.explanation: With symmetric keys, each pair of servers needs its own key: C(10, 2) = 10 x 9 / 2 = 45 keys. With public-key cryptography, each server needs only one key pair (a public and a private key), so 10 pairs = 20 keys in total. This is why asymmetric cryptography scales better.
solution.shortcut: Symmetric grows as n^2/2; asymmetric grows as 2n.
solution.why_others_wrong: 90 counts every ordered pair twice. 10 or 20 secret keys are too few for every pair to have its own key. 45 public keys confuses the two schemes.
solution.final_answer: Option C: 45 secret keys with symmetric encryption; 20 keys (10 key pairs) with public-key encryption

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A simple stream cipher encrypts by XOR-ing each plaintext bit with a key bit. If the plaintext byte is 10110011 and the key byte is 01101010, what is the ciphertext?

solution.explanation: XOR gives 1 when the two bits differ and 0 when they are equal. 10110011 XOR 01101010 = 11011001. XOR-ing the ciphertext with the same key gives back the plaintext, which is why XOR is used in stream ciphers and the one-time pad.
solution.why_others_wrong: 11111011 is the OR of the two bytes, 00100010 the AND, and 00100110 the XNOR (inverted XOR).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text:
Refer to the Loans table. How many rows does this query count?
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Loans WHERE status = 'Active' AND amount > 1000000;

solution.explanation: With AND, a row is counted only if both conditions are true. Active loans are L1, L3, L4, L5 and L8; of these, amount > 10,00,000 holds for L1 (25,00,000), L4 (18,00,000) and L5 (32,00,000). Count = 3.
steps: Active: L1, L3, L4, L5, L8
Of these, amount > 1000000: L1, L4, L5
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 counts all Active loans (or uses OR). 8 counts every row. 2 misses one qualifying loan.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text:
Refer to the Loans table. What value of total appears in the FIRST row returned by this query?
SELECT branch, SUM(amount) AS total FROM Loans GROUP BY branch ORDER BY total DESC;

solution.concept: GROUP BY with SUM and ORDER BY
solution.explanation: GROUP BY makes one row per branch with the sum of its loan amounts: Pune 25,00,000 + 6,50,000 + 1,50,000 = 33,00,000; Delhi 8,00,000 + 32,00,000 + 2,00,000 = 42,00,000; Agra 18,00,000 + 9,00,000 = 27,00,000. ORDER BY total DESC puts the largest first: Delhi with 4,200,000.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3,300,000 is Pune's total (second row). 2,700,000 is Agra's (last row). 3,200,000 is the largest single loan, not a branch total.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text:
Refer to the Loans table. How many rows does this query count?
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Loans WHERE type = 'Car' OR type = 'Home' AND status = 'Active';

solution.explanation: In SQL, AND binds more tightly than OR, so the condition means type = 'Car' OR (type = 'Home' AND status = 'Active'). Car loans: L2, L3, L7 (any status). Active Home loans: L1, L4, L5. Total = 6. To count only active Car or Home loans, brackets are needed: (type = 'Car' OR type = 'Home') AND status = 'Active', which gives 4.
steps: Read as: Car OR (Home AND Active)
Home and Active: L1, L4, L5 = 3
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 assumes the OR is evaluated first. 1 counts only active Car loans. 8 counts every row.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: While designing a database for a bank, an analyst draws an E-R (Entity-Relationship) diagram. In the standard notation, which shape represents an entity set such as Customer or Account?

solution.explanation: In Chen's E-R notation, entity sets are rectangles, relationships are diamonds, attributes are ellipses and multivalued attributes are double ellipses.
solution.why_others_wrong: A diamond shows a relationship (e.g. Holds), an ellipse an attribute (e.g. Name), and a double ellipse a multivalued attribute (e.g. several phone numbers).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In a bank's database, one customer can hold many accounts, but each account belongs to exactly one customer. What type of relationship exists between Customer and Account?

solution.explanation: One customer row is linked to many account rows, and each account row to one customer: one-to-many. It is implemented by putting the customer's primary key as a foreign key in the Account table.
steps: Customer -> many accounts; account -> one customer = one-to-many
solution.why_others_wrong: One-to-one would allow only one account per customer. Many-to-many would let an account belong to many customers. The two tables are clearly related.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text:
Table Branch has 5 rows; the manager column is NULL in 2 of them and holds a name in the other 3. What does this query return?
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Branch WHERE manager = NULL;

solution.explanation: NULL means an unknown value, so manager = NULL is never true; it evaluates to UNKNOWN for every row, and WHERE keeps only rows where the condition is true. The count is 0. The correct test is WHERE manager IS NULL, which would return 2.
steps: Any comparison with NULL using = gives UNKNOWN
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 is the answer for IS NULL. 3 counts rows with a manager. 5 counts every row.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the Excel sheet. What does =AVERAGEIF(B2:B7, "Pune", C2:C7) return?

solution.explanation: AVERAGEIF averages the cells of C2:C7 whose matching cell in B2:B7 is 'Pune': 48, 55 and 41. (48 + 55 + 41) / 3 = 144 / 3 = 48.
solution.why_others_wrong: 56.33 is the average of all six values. 144 is the SUMIF result. 3 is the COUNTIF result.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft: AVERAGEIF returns the average (arithmetic mean) of all the cells in a range that meet a given criteria; syntax AVERAGEIF(range, criteria, [average_range]).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the Excel sheet. What does =RANK.EQ(C3, C2:C7) return?

solution.explanation: With the order argument omitted, RANK.EQ ranks in descending order. C3 = 62. Only one value (70) is larger, so 62 gets rank 2. John's 62 is tied and also gets rank 2 (tied values share the top rank of the group); the next value, 55, gets rank 4.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2.5 is what RANK.AVG gives for the tie. 3 would skip the tie rule. 4 is the rank in ascending order.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft RANK.EQ: if order is 0 or omitted, Excel ranks number as if ref were sorted in descending order; if more than one value has the same rank, the top rank of that set is returned.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the Excel sheet. What does =COUNTIF(C2:C7, ">"&AVERAGE(C2:C7)) return?

solution.explanation: The & operator joins ">" with the result of AVERAGE(C2:C7) = 338 / 6 = 56.33, giving the criterion ">56.33". Values above it are 62, 62 and 70, so the count is 3.
solution.shortcut: Put the operator in quotes and join the calculated value with &.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0 is what you get if the whole criterion is typed as text ">AVERAGE(C2:C7)", which matches nothing. 2 counts the tied 62s only once. 4 wrongly includes 55.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft COUNTIF: in =COUNTIF(B2:B5,"<>"&B4) the ampersand merges the comparison operator with the value in B4.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A clerk wants the bank's name and the document title to appear automatically at the top of every page of a 30-page Word report. Which feature should she use?

solution.explanation: A header is an area in the top margin whose content repeats on every page (or every page of a section). A footer does the same at the bottom.
steps: Same text at the top of every page = header
solution.why_others_wrong: A footnote is a note at the bottom of one page tied to a reference mark. A watermark is faint text or an image behind the page text. A page break starts a new page.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In a loan-entry sheet, the Branch column must accept only Pune, Delhi or Agra, chosen from a drop-down list, so that clerks cannot type wrong names. Which Excel feature should be applied to the column?

solution.explanation: Data Validation (Data tab) restricts what can be entered in cells, for example a list of allowed values shown as a drop-down, a number range or a date range, and shows an error for invalid entries.
steps: Allow only listed values with a drop-down = Data Validation (List)
solution.why_others_wrong: Conditional Formatting only changes how cells look. Freeze Panes keeps rows or columns visible while scrolling. Goal Seek finds an input value for a target result.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft: use data validation to restrict the type of data or the values that users enter into a cell, like a dropdown list.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A 120-page credit-policy document must have a contents page listing every chapter and section with its page number, which can be refreshed after the text is edited. What must be done to the chapter and section titles so that Word can build this automatically?

options.text: Type them in bold capital letters
Format them with built-in Heading styles (Heading 1, Heading 2 ...)
Insert a page break before each of them
Add each of them as a footnote

solution.explanation: Word builds an automatic table of contents from text formatted with Heading styles. After edits, Update Table refreshes the entries and page numbers.
steps: Apply Heading styles -> References > Table of Contents -> update when needed
solution.why_others_wrong: Bold capitals only change appearance; Word does not treat them as headings. Page breaks and footnotes do not mark text as headings.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Format them with built-in Heading styles (Heading 1, Heading 2 ...)

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft: Word uses the headings in your document to build an automatic table of contents that can be updated when you change the heading text, sequence or level.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A1 contains the date 15-Jan-2026 and B1 contains 15-Apr-2026. C1 holds =B1-A1 and is formatted as Number with no decimals. What does C1 show?

solution.explanation: Excel stores dates as serial numbers (one per day), so subtracting two dates gives the number of days between them. Jan 15 to Apr 15, 2026 = 16 (rest of January) + 28 (February 2026 is not a leap year) + 31 (March) + 15 (April) = 90 days.
solution.why_others_wrong: 91 counts both the start and the end date, or treats February 2026 as having 29 days. 89 and 92 come from other month-length slips.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft DATE function: Excel stores dates as sequential serial numbers so that they can be used in calculations; January 1, 1900 is serial number 1.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank wants a PowerPoint presentation about its deposit schemes to play by itself in a loop on a screen in the branch lobby, with full-screen display and no presenter, until someone presses Esc. Which Set Up Slide Show option should be chosen?

solution.explanation: 'Browsed at a kiosk (full screen)' loops the slide show until Esc is pressed and stops viewers from changing slides by clicking; slides should have rehearsed timings so they advance automatically.
steps: Unattended, looping, full screen = Browsed at a kiosk
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Presented by a speaker' expects a presenter to advance slides. 'Browsed by an individual' opens the show in a window. Presenter View shows notes to a speaker on a second screen.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Browsed at a kiosk (full screen)

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft: Browsed at a kiosk (full screen) loops your slide show until the person watching presses Esc.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: After scanning a merchant's QR code and entering the amount in a UPI app, what secret does the customer enter to authorise the payment from his bank account?

solution.explanation: Every standard UPI payment is authorised with the UPI PIN, a secret number set by the customer for the linked bank account. It should never be shared, and it is not needed to receive money.
solution.why_others_wrong: The CVV is used for card payments. The IFSC identifies a bank branch and is not secret. A customer ID is an identifier, not a payment authorisation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A customer loads a small balance into an on-device wallet in her UPI app so that she can make quick, small-value payments (such as for tea or bus tickets) without entering the UPI PIN for each one. Which NPCI feature is this?

solution.explanation: UPI Lite is an on-device wallet for small-value UPI payments. Money is loaded into it (with the UPI PIN), and small payments from it do not need the PIN each time, which also reduces load on banks' core systems.
steps: On-device wallet, small payments without PIN = UPI Lite
solution.why_others_wrong: UPI 123PAY is UPI for feature phones. AePS allows Aadhaar-and-biometric transactions at micro-ATMs. NACH handles bulk and recurring debits and credits.

fact_checks.claim: NPCI circular UPI OC 138 introduced UPI Lite, an on-device wallet for small-value transactions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An online shop wants to accept card and net-banking payments. It needs a service that securely carries the customer's payment details from its checkout page to the banks and card networks for authorisation and returns the result to the website. What is this service called?

solution.explanation: A payment gateway is the technology layer between a merchant's website or app and the acquiring bank / card networks. It encrypts and forwards payment data for authorisation and sends the approval or decline back.
steps: Carries payment data from website to banks and back = payment gateway
solution.why_others_wrong: A DNS server maps names to IP addresses. A CDN serves website files from nearby servers. A browser is the customer's software for viewing pages.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Under the ISO/IEC 7812 numbering scheme, the leading digits of a payment card number identify the institution that issued the card, which lets a terminal route the transaction to the right network and issuer. What are these leading digits called?

options.text: Issuer Identification Number (IIN), also called BIN

solution.explanation: A card number begins with the IIN (often called the Bank Identification Number, BIN), whose first digit is the Major Industry Identifier. Then come the issuer-assigned account digits, and the last digit is the Luhn check digit.
steps: Leading digits that identify the issuer = IIN / BIN
solution.why_others_wrong: The CVV is a separate security code, not part of the card number. The PIN is a secret known only to the cardholder. The IBAN is an international bank account number format, not a card number part.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Issuer Identification Number (IIN), also called BIN

fact_checks.claim: ISO/IEC 7812: the first six or eight digits of a card number, including the major industry identifier, compose the issuer identification number (IIN), which identifies the issuing organisation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A shop that accepts debit and credit cards finds that, for each card sale, its bank keeps a small percentage of the amount as a fee before crediting the rest to the shop's account. What is this fee called?

solution.explanation: The MDR is charged to the merchant by the acquiring bank for card-payment services, usually as a percentage of the transaction amount. It is shared among the acquirer, the issuer (interchange) and the card network.
steps: Fee a merchant pays its bank per card transaction = MDR
solution.why_others_wrong: MSF and CRR are RBI monetary-policy instruments for banks, not merchant fees. 'Interchange Settlement Number' is not a payment term.

fact_checks.claim: MDR is the fee charged to a merchant by a bank for providing debit and credit card payment facilities, usually a percentage of the transaction amount.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: The firmware of a computer is stored in ROM, whose contents are not lost when the power is switched off. What does ROM stand for?

solution.explanation: ROM (Read-Only Memory) is non-volatile memory whose contents are written at manufacture or by special programming, and are normally only read during use.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: At an ATM, a customer types a secret 4-digit number to prove that the card is his. This number is the PIN. What does PIN stand for?

solution.explanation: A PIN (Personal Identification Number) is a secret numeric code that authenticates the cardholder ('something you know').
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Every device on the internet is given an IP address, such as 192.168.1.10. What does IP stand for here?

solution.explanation: IP (Internet Protocol) is the network-layer protocol that addresses and routes packets between networks; an IP address identifies a device's network interface.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: The internet service that converts a website name such as www.bank.example into its IP address is DNS. What does DNS stand for?

solution.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) is the distributed, hierarchical directory that maps domain names to IP addresses and other records.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank uses CRM software to record every customer's enquiries, complaints and product holdings so that relationship managers can offer suitable products. What does CRM stand for?

solution.explanation: CRM (Customer Relationship Management) software manages an organisation's interactions with its customers: contact history, leads, service requests and sales opportunities.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are not what CRM means in business software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Because of CBS, a customer can deposit or withdraw money at any branch of his bank, not only at his home branch, since all branches work on one centralised system. What does CBS stand for?

solution.explanation: CBS (Core Banking Solution) runs a bank's accounts and transactions on central servers in a data centre, so every branch and channel works on the same up-to-date data ('anywhere banking').
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: SIM swap fraud tricks a mobile operator into issuing a new SIM for a customer's number. What does SIM stand for?

solution.explanation: The SIM (Subscriber Identity Module) card securely stores the subscriber's identity and keys that the mobile network uses to authenticate the phone number.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank uses ERP software to run its internal functions, such as HR, payroll, procurement and fixed-asset accounting, on one integrated system. What does ERP stand for?

solution.explanation: ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) software integrates an organisation's core business processes (finance, HR, purchasing, inventory) around one shared database.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Email was designed for plain text; the standard that lets an email carry attachments such as PDF statements, images and non-English text is MIME. What does MIME stand for?

solution.explanation: MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) defines how email messages carry non-text attachments, multiple parts and character sets. Its media types (such as application/pdf) are also used on the web.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank's network team monitors the status, traffic and errors of all its routers and switches from one console using the SNMP protocol. What does SNMP stand for?

solution.explanation: SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) lets a management station read and set information on network devices and receive alerts (traps) from them.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Simple Network Management Protocol
